item.title: Asahikawa Winter Festival Guide: Snow Sculptures & Zoo
item.description: Hokkaido’s second city, Asahikawa, is one of Japan’s coldest places — and it embraces winter wholeheartedly. Each February, the Asahikawa Winter Festival raises some of the largest snow sculptures in Japan (it has held world records), with huge snow stages, slides and illuminations along the Ishikari River and downtown. The city is also home to the wildly popular Asahiyama Zoo, famous for its winter penguin walk, and is a hub for Asahikawa-style soy ramen and a gateway to the Daisetsuzan mountains.

item.title: Hokkaido Family Trip: Snow Activities, Farms, Bears & Kid-Friendly Hokkaido
item.description: Hokkaido offers something that Japan’s urban destinations cannot: space and nature at a scale that makes sense to children. An animal walking toward you in the wild, a penguin that passes at eye level on a bridge, a dairy farm where you watch a cow being milked and drink the milk 30 minutes later — these experiences have a directness that theme park rides approximate but cannot replicate. This guide covers Hokkaido’s family-specific attractions with practical detail on what works for different age groups.
